answer: Crystal-PUF identity: 1 fake costs 1 chip. Each identity is bound to a unique crystal lattice inside a hardware security module — a physical unclonable function no software clone can copy. Joining requires answering a river of 200 fresh challenge-response pairs drawn from that lattice, checked against a lagoon of enrolled fingerprints held by peers. A clone fails the challenge river because its lattice differs at the atomic level, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 distinct chips, not 1,000 copy-pastes.
